v1_location: CONTRACT v1 §2 'Competing records are retained as an explicitly related set'
v1_statement_or_label: "Genuinely duplicate encodings do not occur in this cache."
v2_statement_or_label: "No competing set is identical on every preserved identity field. That establishes NON-IDENTICAL ENCODINGS. It does not establish that duplicate encodings are absent: two records may encode one measurement in different words."
why: The check compares preserved strings. Different strings do not prove different measurements.

v1_statement_or_label: "every one of them is a distinct outcome, time point or population rather than a re-encoding of the same measurement"
v2_statement_or_label: "Each of the 4,464 competing sets differs on at least one preserved field, so its members are non-identical encodings. Whether they are distinct outcomes, time points or populations is UNRESOLVED for all 4,464."
why: Same root: encoding difference was read as measurement difference.

v1_statement_or_label: "competing measures are identical on every preserved identity field - a genuinely duplicate encoding rather than a distinct outcome. Observed count: 0"
v2_statement_or_label: IDENTICAL_ON_ALL_PRESERVED_FIELDS__SEMANTIC_DUPLICATION_UNRESOLVED: "identical on every preserved field. Observed count 0. Its absence says nothing about semantic duplication, which is a separate, unresolved question."
why: The label named a semantic conclusion the field comparison cannot reach.
States what the comparison shows and leaves the semantics open.

v2_statement_or_label: distinction_basis: TEXT_DERIVED_ONLY (1,744 sets) vs INCLUDES_STRUCTURED_FIELD (2,720 sets); DISTINCTION_IS_TEXT_DERIVED_ONLY token in v2_unresolved_states
why: 1,744 of the 4,464 sets are separated only by free-text-derived fields - exactly the case the negative control shows is not evidence of a distinct measurement. No set is merged or normalised.

v1_location: GROUP-RELATIONS v1 column relation_type = POOLED_PARENT_WITH_COMPONENTS (47 rows)
v1_statement_or_label: relation asserted wherever the normalised parent title matched a pooled-word regex
why: A pooled-sounding name is not evidence of who the patients are; where a record field states the pooling, that field and its verbatim text are recorded.

v1_location: CONTRACT v1 §3 and GROUP-RELATIONS v1 arithmetic_note
v1_statement_or_label: "parent and components are the SAME people and are never added together"
v2_statement_or_label: The never-added-together half is KEPT unchanged. The same-people half becomes a per-row same_patients_claim: NOT ESTABLISHED for the 26 name-only rows; SOURCE_STATED, for the components the record names, for the 11 enumerated rows; scope-limited for the 10 superset-language rows.
why: Never adding them is a safe policy; asserting identity of patients from a name is not.

v1_location: CONTRACT v1 §3 conflict table and prose
v1_statement_or_label: table lists 70 WITHIN_MEASURE_SUM_EXCEEDS_ENROLLMENT with 35 indented beneath it; prose says "only 106 trials exceed enrollment, 35 of them ... and only 1 ..."
v2_statement_or_label: The schema's three exact labels are DISJOINT: 70 plain, 35 pooled-label, 1 single-cohort. 106 is the non-exclusive MEMBERSHIP view (any within-measure excess) and is their union. The v1 indentation reads as if 35 were a subset of 70; it is not.
why: 70 and 106 were used in one paragraph as if comparable, and the 35 was presented as nested.

disposition: KEPT, with its arithmetic made explicit
v2_statement_or_label: That measure holds exactly ONE group, so its within-measure 'sum' IS the single cohort, not an additional summation phenomenon. The 41-vs-34 conflict stands as recorded; no field is declared wrong.
why: Prevents the 1 being read as a second, independent excess inside the 106.

v1_statement_or_label: "Each set differs on a real field ... so a preference would be a scientific decision the source does not license."
v2_statement_or_label: Each set differs on at least one preserved field. For 1,744 sets that difference is text-derived only. Neither the choice among records NOR the question of whether they are the same measurement is decidable here.
why: v1 conceded only that selection is undecidable; semantic duplication was treated as settled.

v1_location: CONTRACT v1 §2 denominator table header wording and SCHEMA v1 denominator_state
v1_statement_or_label: "denominator usability" used without stating whose scope it is
v2_statement_or_label: "Denominator usable" = a positive reported Participants denominator AT THIS COMPONENT'S SCOPE. It is NOT a statement of eligibility, of analysis-population membership, or of fitness for any downstream estimand.
why: The word 'usable' invited reading as full eligibility.

v1_location: SCHEMA v1 reporting_status_state.ABSENT_FIELD and ledger noncollection_statement
v1_statement_or_label: both feed the same unusable_reason string
v2_statement_or_label: Source non-collection (639 observations with a verbatim non-collection/termination statement) and an absent reportingStatus field (15 observations, 10 trials) are two different metadata states and are never collapsed into one another or into a missing value.
why: Restates a separation v1 implemented but did not state as a rule.

v2_statement_or_label: negative_control.py + artifacts/NEGATIVE-CONTROL-wording-only-duplicate.json: one synthetic record entered twice with harmless wording differences
why: v1's rule reports no duplicate candidate for it, so v1's sentence would call one record twice 'a distinct outcome, time point or population'. v2 labels it NON_IDENTICAL_ENCODING / TEXT_DERIVED_ONLY / semantics UNRESOLVED. Neither rule merges either record.
